entities.text: High Court Of Delhi At New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C ) has been filed by petitioners seeking quashing of the FIR bearing No. 325/2018, registered at Police Station Dwarka South, New Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 354/354A/323/341/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC ) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Naresh Kumar Chahar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

3. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Rajendra Kumar Tiwari and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Sandeep Kumar from Police Station Dwarka South,
New Delhi.
4.
Brief facts of the present case are that on 04.12.2017, the marriage was solemnized between petitioner and respondent no. 2, according to Hindu Rites and Ceremony.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.

Due to matrimonial disputes, the parties could not stay together and started living Aswani Kumar@Ashwani Bairagi@Rinku & ... vs The State (Nct Of Delhi) Through Sho Ps ... on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18943801/
1 separately since 28.03.2018.

sentences.text:
On the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR bearing No.
325/2018 was registered at Police Station Dwarka South, New Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 354/354A/323/341/506/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

It is stated that on 21.10.2018, on the complaint of respondent no. 2, one more FIR bearing no. 383/2018 was registered at Police Station Palam Village, New Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

entities.text: Police Station Palam Village, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is stated that during the pendency of the case, the parties have amicable settled all their disputes before Mediation Centre, Dwarka Court, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 07.06.2022.
5.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Dwarka Court, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2, who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into a compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before Mediation Centre, Dwarka Court, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 07.06.2022.
6.

It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner.

7. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 8,00,000/- in four installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 3,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 3,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 in the second motion petition.

c. Third installment of Rs. 1,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR bearing No. 383/2018, registered at Police Station, P.S. Palam Vilalge, New Delhi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of IPC.
c. Fourth/Final installment of Rs. 1,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the present FIR before the Hon ble High Court at New Delhi.
8.

Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final installment of Rs. 1,00,000/- today, i.e., 19.04.2023 vide DD No. 300582 drawn on State Bank of India and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

9. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter,
this Court is of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.

11. The present petition stands disposed of.
